text:
The Pauli matrices (scaled by \(\hbar/2\)) are  

\[
P_x=\frac{\hbar}{2}\sigma_x,\qquad 
P_y=\frac{\hbar}{2}\sigma_y,\qquad 
P_z=\frac{\hbar}{2}\sigma_z .
\]

For a direction \(\vec n\) that lies in the \(x\!-\!z\) plane we can write  

\[
\vec n=(\sin\theta,0,\cos\theta),
\]

so the component of \(\vec P\) along \(\vec n\) is  

\[
\vec P\!\cdot\!\vec n =\frac{\hbar}{2}\bigl(\sigma_x\sin\theta+\sigma_z\cos\theta\bigr)
\equiv\frac{\hbar}{2}M .
\]

The eigenvalue problem for eigenvalue \(+\hbar/2\) reduces to  

\[
M\;|\psi\rangle = +1\;|\psi\rangle .
\]

Using the explicit matrices  

\[
\sigma_x=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad
\sigma_z=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix},
\]

\[
M=\sin\theta\,\sigma_x+\cos\theta\,\sigma_z=
\begin{pmatrix}
\cos\theta & \sin\theta\\
\sin\theta & -\cos\theta
\end{pmatrix}.
\]

Let \(|\psi\rangle=(a,b)^{T}\). Solving \((M-I)(a,b)^{T}=0\) gives  

\[
(\cos\theta-1)a+\sin\theta\,b=0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
b=\frac{1-\cos\theta}{\sin\theta}\,a
      =\tan\frac{\theta}{2}\,a .
\]

Choosing the normalization \( |a|^{2}+|b|^{2}=1\) yields  

\[
a=\cos\frac{\theta}{2},\qquad b=\sin\frac{\theta}{2}.
\]

Thus the normalized eigenvector for eigenvalue \(+\hbar/2\) is  

\[
|\psi_{+}\rangle =\bigl(\cos\frac{\theta}{2},\; \sin\frac{\theta}{2}\bigr)^{T}.
\]

This matches option **(B)**.

**Answer: B**
